item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 26 July 2026
item.description:
Shintar mourns World of Warcraft’s short-lived Decor Duels and uses the shutdown to gripe about Blizzard calling content evergreen while PvP queues languish.

Wilhelm and his daughter push Stardew Valley through winter, unlocking the quarry and mine carts, hitting mine level 120, and suffering through all that fishing.

Michael celebrates Llamasoft’s Moose Life as a trippy, ceiling-flipping arcade shooter that feels uniquely its own, even among Jeff Minter’s usual riffs.

Roger says Cold Storage looks like disposable sci-fi horror, but David Koepp’s fungus outbreak thriller turns out to be a modestly fun evening watch.

Bhagpuss rounds up a music-heavy week, arguing Charli xcx’s B-sides like “If You Take Away The Music” and “Playboy Bunny” outshine the singles.

Ramen Junkie’s week mixes confusing World Cup stoppage time, a pricey tire blowout, and small retail wins like vinyl hunting and passing on Leader Laser Prime.

Tipa turns mountain-spotting into a geography puzzle, climbing Heublein Tower to figure out which Connecticut peaks are actually visible from her desk.

Brennan argues the IndieWeb needs real Quebec French terminology, not just borrowed English, to lower barriers and make the scene feel less anglophone by default.

Jamie Zawinski blasts the dependence on Instagram and X after Meta briefly suspended The Stud’s account, warning against outsourcing critical communications to hostile platforms.

Dave Winer pitches the web’s open ethos, notes RSS.chat now has a REST API, and shares code, docs, and an example blog-builder app.

UltrViolet checks in on chemo side effects, dunks on Dungeon Crawler Carl’s non-ending and audiobook voice, and wrestles with AI-image tensions around Blaugust.

Ghastly gives a friendly Blaugust 2026 primer, pitching August blogging, community participation, and the event’s role in honoring Belghast’s legacy.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 25 July 2026
item.description:
Tipa compares her dense, bustling Pokopia island with her daughter’s serene utopia, musing on how our game worlds reflect who we are.

Shintar loved SWTOR’s Legacy Reborn update, praising its character moments, big Star Wars feels, and the lack of KOTOR-style cutscenes.

Owls is rolling into EverQuest Legends on Freeport with a shadow knight/necromancer/shaman, sold on multiclassing and a more solo-friendly Norrath.

Scopique walks through his Star Citizen fleet, from mining rigs and cargo tools to homestead defense and a couple of niche combat ships.

David’s Gunderholfen session sends rival guilds chasing the Ravens through sabotaged dungeon paths before a swamp basilisk crashes the party.

Wilhelm rounds up EverQuest news, from EverQuest Legends launching July 28 to the Lethar TLP server starting with The Serpent’s Spine.

The Chronicler spotlights Baltic Empires, a GMT strategic wargame where asymmetric powers vie for Baltic dominance through war, trade, and state-building.

Andrew Plotkin shares Witness feelie scans and a fun correction: the matchbook’s “long life” symbol turned out to be real Chinese, not a fake gag.

Anarchae checks in on work, budgets, Blaugust plans, Zelda, TV, and anthology reading while bracing for the resume-and-cover-letter grind.

Jimmy points readers to a new Analog Antiquarian piece on Richard III, a quick cross-link for the history-minded.

JJM argues his stalled gamedev projects happen when he chases cool engine code instead of building an actual game first.

Jeromai pivots from a GPT-4o letter about society to Blaugust, blogging, and “claudefishing” as a murky Claude-adjacent Substack trend.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 24 July 2026
item.description:
Stargrace pushes mining past 90 in Wurm Online, turns 9,000 slate shards into castle bricks, and eyes a 10-story build next.

Tipa rethinks her EverQuest Legends live build after beta surprises, landing on a dwarf cleric/shadow knight and wrestling with race, training, and duo roles.

Nimgimli wonders if souls-likes have crowded out approachable action games, arguing Elden Ring-style challenge leaves less room for Spiderman or God of War fans.

Frostilyte finds Echoes From Ciudadela an uneven first-person puzzle adventure, more promising foundation than breakout, with puzzle design that too often misses.

Sey rounds up Tower of Dreams, OFFBEAT, Mina the Hollower vinyl, and a Cult of the Lamb board game with plenty of soundtrack enthusiasm.

Kimimi celebrates Mortal Kombat II as a sequel-event, praising Shao Kahn’s menace, story-forward roster changes, and the thrill of secrets like Jade and Noob Saibot.

Wilhelm hits Windrose’s newly unlocked swamp, where Valheim-style progression, gear upgrades, and one very bad water-filled shovel hole steal the show.

Tobold digs into how Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous uses scarce rests at Drezen to make D&D-style daily powers and party composition matter more.

Warner argues computing’s growing segmentation leaves many seniors frustrated by apps, subscriptions, AI, and tech that feels costly, mandatory, and untrustworthy.

Bruce Schneier argues AI needs a “Genie coefficient” to measure how well agents grasp implied human intent, not just complete tasks.

Dave Winer adds inline images to rss.chat, patches a security issue, and notes Claude can help spot and fix vulnerabilities fast.

Juhis makes the case for forums over fast chat, arguing Signal-style discussions vanish too quickly for writers juggling multiple ongoing conversations.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Thursday, 23 July 2026
item.description:
Azuriel finds Palworld 1.0 still the same compulsive ARK-like loop, only smoother, busier, and good enough to crowd out Hearthstone and Guild Wars 2.

Magi flags Volcano Princess hitting consoles and mobile July 30 with updated translations, voice acting, new content, and a free Steam update later.

Krista spotlights Tiny Delivery, a cosy narrative game about a tiny robot making deliveries while borrowing, meddling, and causing a little chaos.

Joar checks back into WoW with warlock progress, Zul'Aman renown, gathering professions, Loremaster work, and a comically stubborn lack of purple pants.

Marc revisits The House of the Dead and how Sega made zombies, branching paths, and multi-hit enemies stand out in crowded light-gun arcades.

Wilhelm tears into EVE Online’s Ansiblex jump-bridge capacitor changes, arguing the zone-based nullsec nerf turns travel into an unworkable mess.

Roger reflects on retirement by missing the human side of work most: camaraderie, shared knowledge, and the informal help networks AI can’t replace.

UltrViolet does a bullet-point check-in on a quick chemo day, messy InoReader feed cleanup, and barely finding time for Dungeon Crawler Carl.

Jamie Zawinski blasts Scott Wiener over the Trans March fundraising uproar and related pro-Wiener PAC ties, with zero patience for the whole spectacle.

Jeff used Claude to build a GPS time badge for Pimoroni Tufty 2350, then logged Open Sauce satellite data for some neat visualization experiments.

Axxuy rounds up sharp reads on Pandoc link pages, distraction-free writing, PKM skepticism, RSS tradeoffs, and being more public online.

Bhagpuss pivots from making a Zines Forever upload to musing on zines, archiving old work, and why the format still pulls so hard.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 22 July 2026
item.description:
Stargrace is deep in Wurm Online mining grind mode, pushing from 83 toward 99 while juggling meditation and an army of brick-making priests.

Tipa’s Frosthaven crew bungles Spire Basement hilariously, clogging the start with traps and obstacles before chasing a Living Doom kill for her Trapper quest.

Frostilyte marvels at Mewgenics’ absurdly detailed in-game radio, a pointless-on-paper feature that quietly makes the world feel weirdly alive.

Shintar digs through Data for Azeroth and realizes her supposedly casual World of Warcraft playstyle has earned some surprisingly rare achievements.

Tobold argues Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous loses plenty of players to complexity, but that same brutal barrier is exactly where the fun lives.

Joar writes about retirement, moving, and the big unasked questions his sons are really asking sideways about whether he’s okay and whether it was worth it.

Brennan pushes back on vibe coding bravado, arguing AI-generated mountains of code are a maintenance liability, not a meaningful productivity flex.

Warner reads Apple’s rumored device leasing plan as another step toward segmented computing, where financing softens sticker shock but widens who gets access.

Bruce Schneier flags MIT’s rollout of 500-plus AI surveillance cameras with face, object, and behavior classification, and the takeaway is basically just: yikes.

Dave Winer sketches rss.chat as a three-part RSS ecosystem for writing, reading, and whatever indie developers build in the space between.

Wilhelm kicks off Blaugust 2026, keeping Belghast’s blogging tradition alive with the usual signups, Discord, and room for both daily grinders and casual posters.

Blockade85 reflects on building basic self-care habits, surviving summer projects and Poison Everything, and maybe reviving a writing routine before Blaugust.
